Some systems (including MIUI/HyperOS) restrict background apps, which can cut the accessibility event stream and make the overlay come and go. If accessibility is lost, try enabling “Autostart” and setting the battery policy to “No restrictions”. Tested working on HyperOS 3.

How it works: Android has no public API to read another app\'s foreground Activity. This app listens for window state change events through an AccessibilityService. With a debug target selected, it only shows the floating window and records while that app is in the foreground. The floating window uses TYPE_ACCESSIBILITY_OVERLAY, so it needs no draw-over-other-apps permission.
Reads window change events to show the current app package and Activity name in a floating window.
Enable “Current Page” in Accessibility settings, then come back to this app.

The system says the service is enabled, but it is not actually connected. This usually happens when the system recycles the app (common on MIUI/HyperOS). Turn the “Current Page” switch off and on again in Accessibility settings. Also allow autostart and remove battery restrictions to reduce the chance of it happening again.
